# Declare docs

The Declare documentation, rendered as a Declare app — self-hosted: Declare
documenting Declare. It loads `docs/declare-model.json` — the extractor's
output (tools/internal/doc/extract.mjs), one walkable data structure — and
renders three modes over it: the guide, chapter by chapter; the language, one
page per form the grammar accepts; and the class reference, a page per
component with its prose, members, and live examples. A left rail navigates
the mode, a detail pane reads it, and every doc string is rendered by the
runtime's own Markdown component.

`{ }` bodies are TypeScript → `0x…` colors and expressions; `[ ]` literal
slots take `#…` / named colors. Every color reads `theme.<token>` — one
provided record on the App (see it there), so the whole document reskins
from one place.

## Type tokens

Selection is a provided value: these tokens don't opt in themselves — the
detail pane sets `selectable = true` on its container, so all right-pane text
(including Markdown prose) is selectable, while the left rail stays
unselectable chrome.

segments.html:
class Title extends Text [ fontWeight = semibold, textColor = { provided("theme").text } ]

class Muted extends Text [ textColor = { provided("theme").textMuted } ]

class Mono extends Text [ fontFamily = { app.mono } ]

// a component tab in the left rail — selection is one App attribute
// (`app.selected`, the class name); a tab lights when it matches and writes
// the location on click, so the whole navigator is one string

class ClassTab extends View [ width = { parent.width }, height = 30, cornerRadius = 6,
    cname:   string = "",
    lit: boolean = { app.mode == "reference" && app.selected == classroot.cname },
    fill = { lit ? provided("theme").sel : hovered ? provided("theme").control : null },
    link = { "#reference/" + cname },
    onClick()     { app.goRef(classroot.cname) },
    lbl: Mono [ x = 24, y = 7, fontSize = 14, wrap = false,
        text = { classroot.cname },
        textColor = { classroot.lit ? provided("theme").text : provided("theme").tabIdle } ]
    ]

A rail group's head — the line that folds it. A group is OPEN when it holds the
current page, closed otherwise; a click overrides that, and the override holds
until the next navigation (its key is the page it was made on), so folding a
group never fights the rail when you land somewhere new. One class serves the
guide's parts, the language's form groups, and the class groups alike.

segments.html:
class FoldHead extends View [ width = { parent.width }, height = 28, cornerRadius = 6, cursor = "pointer",
    label:    string  = "",
    contains: boolean = false,             // does this group hold the current page?
    manual:   boolean = false,             // the reader's fold, …
    manualAt: string  = "",                // … keyed by the page it was made on
    open:     boolean = { classroot.manualAt == app.page ? classroot.manual : classroot.contains },
    fill = { hovered ? provided("theme").control : null },
    onClick() { manual = !open; manualAt = app.page },
    mark: Mono [ x = 8, y = 8, fontSize = 10, wrap = false, textColor = { provided("theme").textMuted },
        text = { classroot.open ? "\u25BC" : "\u25B6" } ],
    lbl: Text [ x = 24, y = 6, fontSize = 14, fontWeight = semibold, wrap = false,
        text = { classroot.label },
        textColor = { classroot.contains ? provided("theme").text : provided("theme").tabIdle } ]
    ]


// one topic of classes in the reference rail (model.classGroups — extract's CLASS_GROUPS)

class ClassGroup extends View [ width = { parent.width },
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 2 ],
    head: FoldHead [ label = { "" + :name },
        contains = { app.mode == "reference" && (:classes as any[]).some(c => c.name == app.selected) } ],
    body: View [ width = { parent.width }, visible = { classroot.head.open },
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 2 ],
        ClassTab [ datapath = :classes[], cname = :name ],
        g: View [ height = 6 ]
        ]
    ]

## The reference kit

The chips, links, rows, and strips a class page is built from. A chip is a
member name in a tinted pill — attribute teal, method blue, event amber, class
accent — and a class chip is a link: a location write, exactly as a rail tab.
Every row of mixed type is a baseline row (`align = baseline`), and every
composite in one claims its baseline.

segments.html:
class Eyebrow extends Mono [ fontSize = { 11 * app.fontScale }, letterSpacing = 1.2, wrap = false,
    textColor = { provided("theme").eyebrow }
    ]


// a section: a rule above, the heading, one line on what the section holds

class SectionHead extends View [ width = { parent.width },
    head: string = "",
    note: string = "",
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 18 ],
    rule: View [ width = { parent.width }, height = 1, fill = { provided("theme").line } ],
    title: View [ width = { parent.width },
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 4 ],
        Title [ fontSize = { 20 * app.fontScale }, text = { classroot.head } ],
        Muted [ fontSize = { 14 * app.fontScale }, width = { parent.width }, text = { classroot.note } ]
        ]
    ]


class Chip extends View [ height = { 24 * app.fontScale }, cornerRadius = 6,
    baseline: number = { this.lbl.y + this.lbl.baseline },
    label: string = "",
    kind:  "attribute" | "method" | "event" | "class" | "token" = "attribute",
    cls:   string = "",
    width = { this.lbl.width + 16 },
    fill = { hovered && cls != "" ? provided("theme").chipHov
           : kind == "method" ? provided("theme").mchipBg
           : kind == "event"  ? provided("theme").echipBg
           : provided("theme").chipBg },
    cursor = { cls != "" ? "pointer" : "default" },
    link = { cls != "" ? "#reference/" + cls : "" },
    onClick() { if (cls != "") app.goRef(cls) },
    lbl: Mono [ x = 8, y = { 5 * app.fontScale }, fontSize = { 13 * app.fontScale }, wrap = false,
        text = { classroot.label },
        textColor = { classroot.kind == "class"  ? provided("theme").accent
                    : classroot.kind == "method" ? provided("theme").chipBlue
                    : classroot.kind == "event"  ? provided("theme").chipAmber
                    : classroot.kind == "token"  ? provided("theme").code
                    : provided("theme").chipTeal } ]
    ]

segments.md:
## Linked signatures

A type printed in a signature is a NAME, and a name with a page behind it is a
link. `app.typeLoc` answers where a printed type is documented — by name
(`Color`, `Motion`, and every class), or by the TOKEN LIST a named enum prints
as (`left | center | right` is `TextAlign`), which is the spelling the reference
shows and so the spelling matched. A type with no page answers `""` and renders
exactly as it did: the same face, the same tint, no cursor and no link.

`SigRun` is the same answer for a whole signature — `onKeyDown(e: KeyEvent)`,
`set(path: string, v: unknown): void` — split into runs, each identifier that
names a page carrying it and everything between them left alone.

segments.html:
class LocChip extends View [ height = { 24 * app.fontScale }, cornerRadius = 6,
    baseline: number = { this.lbl.y + this.lbl.baseline },
    label: string = "",
    to:    string = "",                    // a docs location ("type/Color", "reference/View"), or "" for no link
    tone:  Color  = { provided("theme").accent },
    width = { this.lbl.width + 16 },
    fill = { hovered && to != "" ? provided("theme").chipHov : provided("theme").chipBg },
    cursor = { to != "" ? "pointer" : "default" },
    link = { to != "" ? "#" + to : "" },
    onClick() { if (to != "") app.goLoc(to) },
    lbl: Mono [ x = 8, y = { 5 * app.fontScale }, fontSize = { 13 * app.fontScale }, wrap = false,
        text = { classroot.label },
        textColor = { classroot.tone } ]
    ]


class SigRun extends View [
    sig:    string = "",
    size:   number = 15,
    weight: number = 400,                  // the hundreds ARE the weight keywords (FontWeight)
    dim:    Color  = { provided("theme").text },   // the colour of every run that is not a link
    parts: Dataset [ contents = { { items: app.typeParts(classroot.sig) } } ],
    width  = { this.run.width },
    height = { this.run.height },
    run: View [ datapath = { classroot.parts.value },
        width = { this.contentWidth }, height = { this.contentHeight },
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 0 ],
        Mono [ datapath = :items[], wrap = false,
            fontSize = { classroot.size * app.fontScale },
            fontWeight = { classroot.weight },
            cursor = { :to != "" ? "pointer" : "default" },
            link = { :to != "" ? "#" + :to : "" },
            onClick() { if (:to != "") app.goLoc("" + :to) },
            textColor = { :to == "" ? classroot.dim
                        : hovered ? provided("theme").accent : provided("theme").accentSecondary },
            text = { "" + :t }
            ]
        ]
    ]


// one step of the ancestry: `→` before every ancestor but the first, then its chip

class Link extends View [
    baseline: number = { this.chip.y + this.chip.baseline },
    width = { this.contentWidth },
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 8, align = baseline ],
    arrow: Mono [ fontSize = { 14 * app.fontScale }, visible = { :arrow }, textColor = { provided("theme").sigDim }, text = "→" ],
    chip:  Chip [ kind = "class", cls = { "" + :name }, label = { "" + :name } ]
    ]


// a section link in the row under the opener: the section's name, its count, and
// the scroll — for the reader who came for a fact and will not scroll to reach it

class JumpLink extends View [
    baseline: number = { this.row.y + this.row.name.y + this.row.name.baseline },
    label: string = "",
    count: number = 0,
    to: View = null,
    height = { 28 * app.fontScale }, cornerRadius = 7, cursor = "pointer",
    width = { this.row.width + 24 },
    fill = { hovered ? provided("theme").chipHov : provided("theme").chipBg },
    onClick() { if (to != null) to.scrollIntoView() },
    row: View [ x = 12, y = { 5 * app.fontScale }, width = { this.contentWidth }, height = { 18 * app.fontScale },
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 6, align = baseline ],
        name: Text [ fontSize = { 13 * app.fontScale }, fontWeight = semibold, wrap = false,
            textColor = { provided("theme").accent }, text = { classroot.label } ],
        n: Mono [ fontSize = { 12 * app.fontScale }, wrap = false, textColor = { provided("theme").sigDim }, text = { "" + classroot.count } ]
        ]
    ]

segments.md:
## The wrapping chip

A chip in an inherited strip is a run of words, each word its own tinted box,
abutting — invisibly one chip while it fits. When the label is wider than the
column the chip takes the whole width and its words wrap inside it, the
continuation rows stepped in by the run's `hangingIndent`. Rounding is the
run's: its first word rounds on the left, its last on the right, every other
edge — a row's cut included — runs square, as an inline code span breaks
across lines. (A single word wider than the column still overflows; breaking
inside a word is the text engine's, not a flow's.)

segments.html:
class WrapChip extends View [
    kind:  "attribute" | "method" | "event" = "attribute",
    cls:   string = "",
    label: string = "",
    n:     number = { app.wordsOf(label).length },

    // wider than the column? then the chip is the column, and its words wrap

    long:  boolean = { measureText(label, ({ fontSize: 13 * app.fontScale, fontFamily: app.mono })).width + 16 > parent.width },
    width  = { long ? parent.width : this.run.contentWidth },
    height = { this.run.contentHeight },
    cursor = "pointer",
    link = { "#reference/" + cls },
    onClick() { app.goRef(cls) },
    words: Dataset [ contents = { { items: app.wordsOf(classroot.label) } } ],   // the words as declared data — a cursor root

    // the run's width never comes from the chip (whose width follows the run's
    // content — a cycle): the column when long, else unbounded, pointer-transparent

    run: View [ width = { classroot.long ? classroot.parent.width : 100000 }, pointerEvents = "none",
        datapath = { classroot.words.value },
        layout: WrappingLayout [ spacing = 0, lineSpacing = 4, hangingIndent = 24 ],
        View [ datapath = :items[], height = { 24 * app.fontScale },
            first: boolean = { :i == 0 },
            last:  boolean = { :i == classroot.n - 1 },
            width = { this.t.width + (first ? 8 : 0) + (last ? 8 : 0) },
            cornerRadius = { [first ? 6 : 0, last ? 6 : 0, last ? 6 : 0, first ? 6 : 0] },
            fill = { classroot.hovered ? provided("theme").chipHov
                   : classroot.kind == "method" ? provided("theme").mchipBg
                   : classroot.kind == "event"  ? provided("theme").echipBg
                   : provided("theme").chipBg },
            t: Mono [ x = { parent.first ? 8 : 0 }, y = { 5 * app.fontScale }, fontSize = { 13 * app.fontScale }, wrap = false,
                text = { "" + :w },
                textColor = { classroot.kind == "method" ? provided("theme").chipBlue
                            : classroot.kind == "event"  ? provided("theme").chipAmber
                            : provided("theme").chipTeal } ]
            ]
        ]
    ]

segments.md:
## Reference rows

One row per documented member. `AttrRow` is an attribute: the signature line
(name : type = default), a long or multi-line default on its own indented line,
the read-only badge, the OVERRIDE line when the class re-defaults
an inherited slot (the ancestor's slot as a link, and what its default was
there), then its prose — for an override, the INTENT. `MethodRow` and
`EventRow` are the method and event forms.

segments.html:
class OverrideLine extends View [ width = { parent.width },
    from:  string = "",
    slot:  string = "",
    was:   string = "",
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 8, align = baseline ],
    Muted [ fontSize = { 13 * app.fontScale }, text = "overrides" ],
    Chip [ kind = "class", cls = { classroot.from }, label = { classroot.from + "." + classroot.slot } ],
    Mono [ fontSize = { 13 * app.fontScale }, textColor = { provided("theme").sigDim }, visible = { classroot.was != "" },
        text = { "was = " + classroot.was } ]
    ]


class AttrRow extends View [ width = { parent.width },
    live:  boolean = false,                 // page-active, threaded down to any inline island

    // a long or multi-line `{ … }` default leaves the signature line and sits on its
    // own, indented — a signature is never truncated and never scrolls

    long: boolean = { ("" + (:default ?? "")).length > 44 || ("" + (:default ?? "")).indexOf("\n") >= 0 || this.longType },

    // a long union type (blendMode's eleven modes) leaves the line the same way and
    // wraps — an unwrapped line wider than the pane would let a click-to-jump scroll
    // the whole page sideways

    longType: boolean = { ("" + :type).length > 56 },

    // the printed type's own page, when it has one — a name, or a named enum's
    // token list. "" (no page) leaves the run exactly as it renders today.

    typeTo: string = { app.typeLoc("" + :type) },
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 6 ],

    sig: View [ width = { parent.width },
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 8, align = baseline ],
        Mono [ fontSize = { 15 * app.fontScale }, fontWeight = semibold, textColor = { provided("theme").text }, text = { :name } ],
        ty: Mono [ fontSize = { 15 * app.fontScale }, visible = { !classroot.longType }, text = { ": " + :type },
            textColor = { classroot.typeTo != "" && this.hovered ? provided("theme").accent : provided("theme").accentSecondary },
            cursor = { classroot.typeTo != "" ? "pointer" : "default" },
            link = { classroot.typeTo != "" ? "#" + classroot.typeTo : "" },
            onClick() { if (classroot.typeTo != "") app.goLoc(classroot.typeTo) }
            ],
        Mono [ fontSize = { 14 * app.fontScale }, textColor = { provided("theme").sigDim }, visible = { !classroot.long },
            text = { :default != null ? "= " + :default : "" } ]
        ],
    longTypeLine: Mono [ x = 24, width = { parent.width - 24 }, fontSize = { 14 * app.fontScale }, lineHeight = 1.45,
        visible = { classroot.longType }, text = { ": " + :type },
        textColor = { classroot.typeTo != "" && this.hovered ? provided("theme").accent : provided("theme").accentSecondary },
        cursor = { classroot.typeTo != "" ? "pointer" : "default" },
        link = { classroot.typeTo != "" ? "#" + classroot.typeTo : "" },
        onClick() { if (classroot.typeTo != "") app.goLoc(classroot.typeTo) }
        ],
    longDefault: Mono [ x = 24, width = { parent.width - 24 }, fontSize = { 13 * app.fontScale }, lineHeight = 1.45, textColor = { provided("theme").sigDim },
        visible = { classroot.long }, text = { "= " + ("" + :default).split("\n").join("\n  ") } ],

    flags: Mono [ fontSize = { 12 * app.fontScale }, textColor = { provided("theme").eyebrow },
        visible = { :readOnly },
        text = { :readOnly ? "read-only" : "" } ],

    OverrideLine [ visible = { :overrides != null }, from = { "" + :overrides.from }, slot = { "" + :name },
        was = { :overrides.was != null ? "" + :overrides.was : "" } ],

    Block [ datapath = :docSegs[], width = { parent.width },
        live = { classroot.live }, tone = { provided("theme").refDim }, lead = 1.6 ]
    ]


// The signature string (`set(path: string, v: unknown): void`) comes whole from
// the model; a `:sig.slice()` would be read as a datapath (the `.` extends
// the path), so the datapath values are captured into plain attributes first
// and sliced in TypeScript.

class MethodRow extends View [ width = { parent.width },
    aname:    string = { :name },
    sigfull:  string = { :signature },
    tailtext: string = { this.sigfull.slice(this.aname.length) },   // "(path: …): void"
    live:     boolean = false,
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 6 ],

    sig: View [ width = { parent.width },
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 0 ],
        Mono [ fontSize = { 15 * app.fontScale }, fontWeight = semibold, textColor = { provided("theme").text }, text = { classroot.aname } ],
        SigRun [ sig = { classroot.tailtext }, size = 15, dim = { provided("theme").mtail } ]
        ],

    OverrideLine [ visible = { :overrides != null }, from = { "" + :overrides.from }, slot = { :name + "()" }, was = "" ],

    Block [ datapath = :docSegs[], width = { parent.width },
        live = { classroot.live }, tone = { provided("theme").refDim }, lead = 1.6 ]
    ]


class EventRow extends View [ width = { parent.width },
    live:  boolean = false,
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 6 ],

    sig: SigRun [ sig = { "" + :signature }, size = 15, weight = 600, dim = { provided("theme").text } ],

    Block [ datapath = :docSegs[], width = { parent.width },
        live = { classroot.live }, tone = { provided("theme").refDim }, lead = 1.6 ]
    ]

## The strips

Per ancestor: what the class inherits (`Strip` — the disclosure, the class as a
link, the member counts, one baseline row, then its one-line lead; open, a chip
cloud of every name, each a link, never the ancestor's prose) and what it reads
from above of its own (`ReadStrip`, under Provided — present only for an
ancestor that reads something).

segments.html:
class ReadStrip extends View [ width = { parent.width }, cornerRadius = 10, visible = { :n > 0 },
    open:  boolean = false,
    cname: string = { "" + :name },
    fill = { provided("theme").surface }, stroke = { stroke(1, provided("theme").line) },
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 0 ],

        fill = { hovered ? provided("theme").chipBg : null },
        onClick() { classroot.open = !classroot.open },
        title: View [ x = 16, y = 10, width = { parent.width - 32 },

            Muted [ fontSize = { 13 * app.fontScale }, wrap = false, text = "from" ],
            Chip [ kind = "class", cls = { classroot.cname }, label = { classroot.cname } ],
            Mono [ fontSize = { 13 * app.fontScale }, wrap = false, textColor = { provided("theme").sigDim },

            Muted [ fontSize = { 13 * app.fontScale }, wrap = false, text = "from" ],
            Chip [ kind = "class", cls = { classroot.cname }, label = { classroot.cname } ],

segments.md:
## The live example

An editable source field beside a running preview — the same machinery as the
homepage's editable demos: a `TextInput` seeded from the demo source that
republishes edits on `app.liveSource`, and an `AppIsland` the host mounts
the compiled child app into. Both are keyed by the class name: the editor
seeds from `app.demoSources[<Class>]` (the server populates this from
apps/docs/demos/), and the island's `program = <Class>` is what the host
wires.

segments.html:
class DocField extends TextInput [ multiline = true, spellcheck = false, wrap = false,
    fontFamily = { app.mono }, fontSize = { 13 * app.fontScale }, textColor = { provided("theme").code },   // 13 = the house code size (PROSE.codeSize)
    editName: string = "",
    src: string = "",

    // Seed the field from the demo source once the subtree exists. (TextInput's
    // `initial` yielding-seed can't be used here: its attach-time guard fires
    // before this field's datapath-sourced `src` constraint is bound, so the seed
    // is skipped. An `onInit` write lands after the model has resolved `src`, and —
    // being an author write, not a constraint — leaves the field freely editable.)

    onInit() { text = src },
    onInput() { app.liveCard = editName; app.liveSource = text }
    ]


// Rendered by datapath replication over the class's 0-or-1 `example` array, so the
// whole island (editor + preview) is constructed only for classes that ship a demo.

class Example extends View [ width = { parent.width },
    cname:  string = { :name },
    elines: number = { :lines },
    esrc:   string = { :source },
    estage: number = { :stageH || 250 },   // extractor-measured stage height — the frame fits the settled app
    live:   boolean = false,             // the parent gates the preview: it mounts only when this is true

    // this island's edit failed to compile (host publishes the report; see RunIsland)

    broken: boolean = { app.liveCard == cname && app.liveReport != "" },
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 0 ],   // the preview frame abuts the code block below, no gap

    // the example's own title and lead (from the demo file's opening comment)

    head: View [ width = { parent.width },

## Inline examples, woven through the prose

Every `declare` code fence in any prose that compiles (as-is, or wrapped in
`App […]`) becomes a `RunIsland`: the source above, its live preview below —
edit and it re-runs. The extractor wrote its source to
`apps/docs/demos/<id>.declare`, so the host seeds and mounts it exactly
like the homepage's demos. `live` (threaded from the page) keeps the
preview's slot empty until its page is the one on screen, so only the visible
page's islands ever compile.

        // guide owes a reader it just told to break something

        rev: View [ y = 5, height = 20, cornerRadius = 6, stroke = { stroke(1, provided("theme").line) },
            x = { parent.width - this.width - 10 },
            width = { this.rlbl.width + 16 },
            fill = { hovered ? provided("theme").control : null },

                        app.liveCard = classroot.rid

Navigation is one string — `location`, the URL fragment. The grammar is
this app's own: `<mode>/<cursor>[@heading]` (`guide/04-tree`,
`reference/Slider`, `guide/04-tree@named-views`). The declared initial is the
default, so a fresh `docs.declare` shows the first guide chapter with a clean
URL. mode/chapter/selected derive from it and are never assigned — every
tab and link writes `location`, back/forward writes it back, state follows
(the single-writer rule; assigning derived state would disconnect history).

segments.html: location = "guide/01-thinking-in-declare",

segments.md:
Cross-mode memory (not a language feature — three plain remembered cursors).
`location` only carries the active mode's cursor, so switching guide↔reference
would forget the other side. The navigation verbs keep these in step and the
mode switch consults them, so returning to a mode lands where you left it.

segments.html:
guideAt: string = "01-thinking-in-declare",              // last guide chapter visited …
    refAt:   string = "View",                  // … and last reference class
    formAt:  string = "",                      // … and last language form ("" = the index)
    typeAt:  string = "Color",                 // … and last type page

    // The three navigation verbs every tab, chip and link calls: remember the
    // cursor for its mode, write the location, start the new page at its top.
    // A view that calls one also declares the same reference as its `link`,
    // so the crawler sees the edge and ⌘-click works; the handler runs first,
    // then the follow.

    goGuide(id: string)  { app.guideAt = id;   app.location = "guide/" + id;     app.showPage() },
    goRef(name: string)  { app.refAt = name;   app.location = "reference/" + name; app.showPage() },
    goForm(slug: string) { app.formAt = slug;  app.location = "language/" + slug; app.showPage() },
    goType(name: string) { app.typeAt = name;  app.location = "type/" + name;     app.showPage() },

    // …and the one verb a generated link calls, since a link's target names its
    // own mode: the model hands out locations ("type/Color", "reference/View"),
    // never a verb to guess at.

    goLoc(loc: string) {
        const mode = loc.split("/")[0], cursor = loc.split("/")[1]
        if (mode == "type") app.goType(cursor)
        else if (mode == "language") app.goForm(cursor)
        else if (mode == "guide") app.goGuide(cursor)
        else app.goRef(cursor)
        },

    // The active view, parsed out of `location` (the anchor stripped first — it
    // selects a viewpoint, not a page). The inactive mode's cursor falls back to its
    // remembered value, so its rail/selection stay put behind the other mode.

    page:     string = { app.location.split("@")[0] },                 // the location less its anchor — the fold heads' key
    mode:     string = { app.page.split("/")[0] || "guide" },
    chapter:  string = { app.mode == "guide" ? (app.page.split("/")[1] || "01-thinking-in-declare") : app.guideAt },
    selected: string = { app.mode == "reference" ? (app.page.split("/")[1] || "View") : app.refAt },
    form:     string = { app.mode == "language" ? (app.page.split("/")[1] || "") : app.formAt },
    tname:    string = { app.mode == "type" ? (app.page.split("/")[1] || app.typeAt) : app.typeAt },

    formName(slug: string) -> string {

## Typed signatures
The model's link index: a printed type name → the location that
documents it (a type page, or a class page for a component type), plus
the token-list spelling a named enum prints as. One lookup answers for
every signature the reference renders, and a name the index does not
carry answers "" — which is what keeps an unlinkable type rendering
exactly as it always did instead of becoming a dead link.

segments.html:
tindex: object = { app.docs.read(["types", "index"]) || ({}) },

    typeLoc(s: string) -> string {
        const idx = app.tindex as any
        const u = idx.unions != null ? idx.unions["" + s] : null
        if (u != null) return "" + u
        const n = idx.link != null ? idx.link["" + s] : null
        return n != null ? "" + n : ""
        },

    // a whole signature, split into runs: each identifier that names a page
    // carries its location, everything between them carries "". A signature
    // that resolves whole (an attribute's type) stays one run, so nothing about
    // its rendering changes.

    typeParts(s: string) -> array {
        const text = "" + s
        const whole = app.typeLoc(text)
        if (whole != "") return [({ i: 0, t: text, to: whole })]
        const out = []
        let i = 0
        for (const p of text.split(/([A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*)/)) {
            if (p == "") continue
            out.push({ i: i, t: p, to: /^[A-Za-z_$]/.test(p) ? app.typeLoc(p) : "" })
            i++
        }
        return out
        },

    fontScale: number = 1.0,                   // reader font-size zoom for the CONTENT pane (the A stepper drives it; nav is fixed)
    themeMode: string = "auto",                // "light" | "auto" | "dark" — the ☀◐☾ switch; auto follows app.dark
    barH: number = 52,                         // the house chrome bar (Viewer/Calendar/Tracker share the height)

## The class page's projections
The model stays normalized — inherited members are never copied into
each class — so the page computes its ancestor views here, from the
tree, per selection: the ancestry as links, each ancestor's strip
(names, types, signatures, its one-line lead, its own reads), and a
label's words for the wrapping chip.

segments.html:
classNode(name: string) -> object { return (app.docs.read(["tree"]) || []).find((c) => c.name == name) || null },

    ancestryOf(name: string) -> array {
        const me = app.classNode(name) as any
        return me == null ? [] : me.chain.slice(1).map((n, i) => ({ name: n, arrow: i > 0 }))
        },

    ancestorsOf(name: string) -> array {
        const me = app.classNode(name) as any
        if (me == null) return []
        return me.chain.slice(1).map((id) => app.classNode(id) as any).filter((c) => c != null).map((c) => ({
            name: c.name, lead: app.plainLead(c.doc || ""),
            reads: c.reads || ({ theme: [], provided: [] }),
            n: c.reads ? c.reads.theme.length + c.reads.provided.length : 0,
            attributes: c.attributes.map((a) => ({ name: a.name, label: a.name + ": " + a.type })),
            methods: c.methods.map((m) => ({ name: m.name, label: m.signature })),
            events: c.events.map((e) => ({ name: e.name, label: e.signature })) }))
        },

    // the first paragraph of a class's prose, as plain text — a strip's one-line lead

    plainLead(md: string) -> string {
        return md.split("\n\n")[0].replace(/\n/g, " ").replace(/\*\*/g, "").replace(/\u0060/g, "").replace(/\*/g, "").replace(/\s*\(docs\/system-design[^)]*\)/g, "").trim()
        },

    hasOverrides(list: array) -> boolean { return (list || []).some((a) => a.overrides != null) },

    // a label's words, each keeping its trailing space, so a run of word chips reads continuously

    wordsOf(label: string) -> array {
        const ws = ("" + label).match(/\S+\s*/g) || [label]
        return ws.map((w, i) => ({ i: i, w: w }))
        },

    // Match + rank + snippet, in one pass per query. Terms AND — every term
    // must appear in title or text. Rank: title prefix > title > body count.
    // The snippet is a word-trimmed window around the first body match, terms
    // bolded for the Markdown row (the snippet text is escaped first, so
    // corpus punctuation cannot leak markup into a result).

    findDocs(q: string, idx: object) -> array {
        const query = ("" + q).trim().toLowerCase()
        const entries = idx != null ? (idx as any).entries : null
        if (query == "" || entries == null) return []
        const terms = query.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)
        const out = []
        for (const e of entries) {
            const tl = e.title.toLowerCase(), xl = e.text.toLowerCase()
            let score = 0, first = -1, ok = true
            for (const t of terms) {
                const ti = tl.indexOf(t), xi = xl.indexOf(t)
                if (ti < 0 && xi < 0) { ok = false; break }
                if (ti >= 0) score += ti == 0 ? 120 : 50
                if (xi >= 0) { score += 10; if (first < 0 || xi < first) first = xi }
            }
            if (!ok) continue
            let snip = ""
            if (first >= 0) {
                let a = Math.max(0, first - 70), b = Math.min(e.text.length, first + 130)
                while (a > 0 && e.text[a - 1] != " ") a--          // trim to word edges
                while (b < e.text.length && e.text[b] != " ") b++
                snip = (a > 0 ? "…" : "") + e.text.slice(a, b) + (b < e.text.length ? "…" : "")
                snip = snip.replace(/([\\\u0060*_[\]<>#|])/g, "\\$1")   // escape before bolding (\u0060 = backtick, an escape so the { } scanner never sees one raw)
                for (const t of terms) {
                    const safe = t.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&")
                    snip = snip.replace(new RegExp(safe, "ig"), (m) => "**" + m + "**")
                }
            }
            out.push({ loc: e.loc, title: e.title, crumb: e.crumb, snip: snip, score: score, i: 0 })
        }
        out.sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)
        const top = out.slice(0, 40)
        for (let i = 0; i < top.length; i++) top[i].i = i   // the row's index — keyboard walk + selection highlight key on it
        return top
        },

The `declare-docs:` resolver — this app's packaging of the one symbolic
link scheme (tools/internal/doc/links.mjs is the registry; the gate keeps
every target real). Guide and reference IDs navigate in-app; the rest
resolve by the same mechanical id→path rule the registry generates them
with, and leave through `navigate`. An ordinary href just navigates.

segments.html:
// A page switch starts at the top of the new page — the detail pane keeps its
    // scroll offset otherwise. The reveal target is a zero-size anchor at the pane's
    // very top, not the column: the column sits 40px into the pane, so aligning its
    // top with the viewport would eat that margin. Every switch path routes through
    // here: rail tabs and prose links alike.

    showPage() { this.detail.top.scrollIntoView() },

    // An in-app doc link is a location write — it navigates the app exactly like
    // a rail tab, so it deep-links, shares, and back-buttons. It also keeps the
    // remembered cursor in step (like the tabs). External schemes still leave
    // through `navigate`.

    openDocLink(href: string) {
        if (!href.startsWith("declare-docs:")) { app.navigate(href); return }
        const id = href.slice("declare-docs:".length)
        if (id.startsWith("guide:")) {                       // guide:tree → the chapter whose id ends with the slug
            const slug = id.slice("guide:".length)
            const hit = (app.docs.read(["guide"]) || []).find(c => c.id.replace(/^\d+-/, "") == slug)
            if (hit) app.goGuide(hit.id)
            return
        }
        if (id == "reference:index") { app.goRef(app.refAt); return }
        if (id.startsWith("language:")) { app.goForm(id.slice("language:".length)); return }   // language:class → the form's page ("language:" alone → the index)
        if (id.startsWith("type:")) { app.goType(id.slice("type:".length)); return }           // type:Motion → the type's page
        if (!id.includes(":")) { app.goRef(id.split(".")[0]); return }                      // a reference symbol: View / View.width
        if (id.startsWith("operational:")) { app.navigate("docs/operational/" + id.slice("operational:".length) + ".md"); return }
        if (id == "spec:core") { app.navigate("docs/declare.md"); return }
        if (id == "essay:why-declare") { app.navigate("apps/homepage/homepage.declare") }
        },

The pill is a View; the input lives in its flat zone. TextInput's
`padding` is uniform (16px of it would crush a 32px field), so the
capsule shape and the text inset split: the wrapper draws the
chrome — surface fill, the themed line that turns accent while the
field inside holds focus — and the field starts exactly where the
cap ends (x = the 16px radius), transparent chrome of its own.
The field's own fill stays the surface tone (it paints only inside
the flat zone, so its square corners are invisible) because the
editable's colorScheme derives from its view's fill — that is what
keeps the native caret and placeholder legible in dark.

The pill centers in the window but never collides: its span is the
gap between the brand and whatever the right cluster starts with
(measured off those views, not a breakpoint — a longer brand or a
wider stepper moves the bound by itself), and the centered x is
clamped into that gap. Below `compact` the stepper stands down (the
reading zoom is the most droppable control; the theme switch and the
search are not), which is what keeps the pill usable at 560.
